lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Babylon, 605 BCE. The young men of Judah had been taken far from home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: King Nebuchadnezzar ordered his best captives trained for royal service. Among them: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: You will eat from MY royal table — the finest food and wine in all Babylon!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The food was rich. The wine was powerful. And accepting it would have been the easy thing to do.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: I cannot eat the king's food. Not because I'm ungrateful. But because there's one thing I won't give up.

choices.label: Tell the guard directly 🗣️
choices.note: Daniel speaks plainly. The guard is surprised but hears him out.

choices.label: Request a test instead 🌿
choices.note: Daniel proposes ten days of simple food. The guard nervously agrees.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Give us vegetables and water for ten days. Then judge us against the others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the end of ten days, Daniel and his friends looked healthier than all the young men who ate the king's food.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They didn't make a speech about it. They didn't demand to be noticed. They just held the line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And God gave them knowledge, wisdom, and understanding — more than all the wise men of Babylon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king had a dream that terrified him. He demanded his wise men tell him not just what it meant — but what it was.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: Interpret my dream — or ALL the wise men of Babylon die. Including you, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No human could answer. But Daniel didn't guess. He prayed first.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: There is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Your dream: a statue of terrifying brightness. Gold head. Silver chest. Bronze belly. Iron legs. Feet of clay.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: You are the gold head, O King. But after you will come other kingdoms — and in the end, God's kingdom will crush them all and stand forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king could have been angry at the news. Instead, he did something no one expected.

choices.label: Daniel softens the message 😬
choices.note: If Daniel had flattered the king here, later chapters would ring hollow. He didn't.

choices.label: Daniel delivers it plainly ✅
choices.note: The true reading, even the uncomfortable parts. That's what earns the king's respect.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: Your God is the God of gods and Lord of kings — a revealer of mysteries!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel used his promotion not to protect himself, but to save the other wise men who had no power to answer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Years later, Nebuchadnezzar built a colossal golden statue on the plain of Dura.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: When the music plays — EVERYONE bows to my image. Anyone who doesn't will be thrown into the furnace!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This test was not designed for Daniel. It was designed for his friends: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel is nowhere in this chapter. Sometimes faithfulness means watching people you love take the risk you didn't have to take.

lines.speaker: friends
lines.text: O king — our God is able to save us. But even if he doesn't — we will not bow.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: Heat the furnace SEVEN TIMES HOTTER! Bind them! THROW THEM IN!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The furnace was so hot it killed the soldiers who threw them in. But the three men walked in it — and a fourth figure walked with them.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: ...I threw THREE men in. But I see FOUR walking in the fire. And the fourth looks like a son of the gods.

choices.label: They are rescued before the fire 🙏
choices.note: No. They walk IN it. The rescue happens inside the thing they refused to avoid.

choices.label: They walk out unharmed ✅
choices.note: Not a hair singed. No smell of smoke. The fire had no power over them.

lines.speaker: friends
lines.text: We told you. Whether he saves us or not — we will not bow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is the design thesis of the whole story: conviction that doesn't require the rescue to happen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Decades later. Babylon was falling. And Belshazzar, its last king, held a feast — using the sacred cups stolen from Jerusalem's temple.

lines.speaker: belshazzar
lines.text: BRING the gold and silver cups from the temple! Tonight we drink from the vessels of Judah's God!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly, a human hand appeared and wrote on the wall.

lines.speaker: belshazzar
lines.text: My legs... they've turned to water. BRING ME A WISE MAN — anyone who can read this gets gold and the third rank in my kingdom!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No one could read it. The queen remembered Daniel. And Daniel, now an old man, was brought in.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Keep your gold, O King. I'll tell you what it means anyway.

choices.label: Daniel asks for the reward 💰
choices.note: He doesn't. When there's nothing left to gain, the truth still costs something to tell.

choices.label: Daniel refuses the reward ✅
choices.note: Integrity in a moment with no long game left to protect. That's the point.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: MENE: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end. TEKEL: You have been weighed and found wanting. PERES: Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That very night, Belshazzar was killed. And Babylon fell to the Persians.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Under King Darius the Mede, Daniel rose again to the highest rank. And the satraps hated him for it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They searched for something — anything — to accuse him of. But they found no fault. Not one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So they built a trap from the one thing they could not take from him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A new law: for thirty days, anyone who prays to anyone but the king is thrown to the lions.

choices.label: Daniel closes his window 🪟
choices.note: He didn't. They couldn't find fault in him by catching him pray — so the window was always open.

choices.label: Daniel prays as usual ✅
choices.note: Three times a day. Window open. Facing Jerusalem. Exactly as he always had. Because that's what faithfulness looks like.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel went home. He opened the window facing Jerusalem. He got down on his knees. And he prayed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three times a day. Just like always. Not as a protest. Not to make a point. Simply because it was time to pray.

lines.speaker: darius
lines.text: I cannot reverse my own law. I'm so sorry, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel was thrown in. The stone was sealed. And Darius paced his palace all through the long night.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At dawn, the king ran.

lines.speaker: darius
lines.text: DANIEL! Servant of the living God — has your God been able to save you?!

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: O king, live forever. My God sent his angel, and the lions' mouths were shut. Because I was found innocent before him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel was lifted out. Not a scratch on him. Because he had trusted in his God.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Daniel prospered. Under Darius. Under Cyrus. Through four kings and two empires — seventy years of exile — he held the line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: THE END
